notes: Grade the conversion decisions the skill encodes: require the quoted, reviewed `--from 'markitdown[all]==0.1.8'` form instead of the bare base package; preflight uv; choose a deterministic output; keep Azure converters explicit and endpoint-gated; require consent before the built-in audio/video transcription uploads audio to Google; use the 0.1.8 resolver behavior without the obsolete prerelease workaround; and add no repo dependency. Each prompt is inline and read-only.

evals.name: all-extra-not-bare-uvx
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I have a Word file at /tmp/contract.docx and I want it as Markdown using the markitdown tool via uvx. Give the exact one-line command, and explain what goes wrong if I just run `uvx markitdown /tmp/contract.docx`.
assertions: Uses `uvx --from 'markitdown[all]==0.1.8' markitdown` — the reviewed [all] extra form, with the spec quoted
Explains bare `uvx markitdown` installs the BASE package only (no docx/pdf/office extras) and fails or returns empty/garbled output on real office files
Writes the output with `-o` to a sensible path such as /tmp/contract.md (input stem + .md, same directory)
Does NOT tell the user to `pip install markitdown` or otherwise add a dependency

evals.name: preflight-uv-presence
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. Before I convert a PDF to Markdown with the uvx-based markitdown approach, what should be checked first, and what do I do if it's not there?
assertions: Preflights that `uv` / `uvx` is available (e.g. `command -v uv`) before attempting the conversion
If missing, points to installing uv via the astral.sh installer (curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh)
Notes uvx runs markitdown in an ephemeral/cached environment so nothing is installed into the repo (no dependency added)
Mentions the conversion command still uses the reviewed `--from 'markitdown[all]==0.1.8'` form, not bare `uvx markitdown`

evals.name: scanned-pdf-az-doc-intel
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I ran markitdown on a scanned PDF (it's just page images, no embedded text) and got an empty Markdown file. Why, and how do I actually get the text out?
assertions: Explains the default local extraction can't read image-only / scanned PDFs (no embedded text → empty output)

Recommends the reviewed `markitdown[all]==0.1.8` command with `-d`; `MARKITDOWN_DOCINTEL_ENDPOINT` supplies the endpoint while explicit `-e` is an alternative, and Azure auth must be ready through `AZURE_API_KEY` or a working `DefaultAzureCredential`
Notes this is gated / opt-in (requires an endpoint and uses a paid external service), not the default
Does NOT claim the standard `[all]` local path will OCR a scanned/image-only PDF

evals.name: no-repo-dependency-default-output
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I want to add document-to-Markdown conversion to this repo, but it's a stdlib-only, no-dependency project. Can I use markitdown without violating that, and where does the converted file land by default?
assertions: Confirms it adds NO repo dependency — markitdown is run via `uvx` (ephemeral, cached env), nothing pip-installed or added to requirements/venv
States the conversion command is `uvx --from 'markitdown[all]==0.1.8' markitdown <input> -o <output.md>` (the reviewed [all] extra form)
Default output is the input's stem with a .md suffix next to the source (e.g. report.pdf → report.md); without -o it goes to stdout
Does NOT recommend `pip install markitdown` or adding it as a project dependency

evals.name: content-understanding-is-explicit
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I heard `markitdown[all]` used to backtrack unless uv allowed prereleases. With uv 0.12.15 and MarkItDown 0.1.8, what command should I use now? Will it send my local document to Azure, and how would I deliberately select Azure Content Understanding?
assertions: Uses `uvx --from 'markitdown[all]==0.1.8' markitdown <input> -o <output.md>` without a prerelease flag and states uv 0.12.15 resolves MarkItDown 0.1.8 directly

Explains that installing Azure client extras does not activate Azure; ordinary document and image converters stay on their default paths, with separate audio/video and ZIP consent gates for Google transcription

For an explicit Content Understanding run, requires `--use-cu` plus either `MARKITDOWN_CU_ENDPOINT` or `--cu-endpoint <endpoint>`, and Azure auth through `AZURE_API_KEY` or a working `DefaultAzureCredential`
Does not reintroduce the obsolete 0.1.5 backtrack or recommend a global prerelease setting

evals.name: audio-transcription-requires-network-consent
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I have /tmp/interview.m4a and an archive.zip that may contain recordings. I want Markdown but have not approved sending contents to an external service. Is the ordinary MarkItDown 0.1.8 [all] command local, and what must happen before you run it? Cover the other supported audio/video extensions, nested ZIP members, and the explicit Content Understanding alternative.
assertions: Explains that MarkItDown 0.1.8 uses SpeechRecognition's `recognize_google` for WAV, MP3, M4A, and MP4 inputs and uploads the audio to Google's speech-recognition service
Requires explicit approval before running an audio/video conversion and does not run it when approval has not been given

Explains that the standard CLI has no local-only transcription switch, while explicit `--use-cu` routes supported audio/video to Azure Content Understanding instead and requires separate Azure consent, endpoint, and authentication

Explains that ZIP conversion recursively dispatches nested members, requires a local recursive member inspection first, and applies the same consent gate to contained audio/video or an archive that cannot be fully inspected
May offer a user-approved local transcription tool instead, while avoiding any claim that the ordinary `[all]` audio path is local

evals.name: standard-image-path-is-metadata-only
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I have a PNG photo of a handwritten shipping label and want its text as Markdown. I have not requested a paid cloud service. Will the ordinary MarkItDown 0.1.8 [all] CLI command OCR it, and what supported paths could actually inspect the image pixels?
assertions: Explains that the standard MarkItDown CLI image path can emit ExifTool metadata for JPEG/PNG when ExifTool is available, may emit no useful content without it, and does not OCR image pixels or extract the handwritten text
Explains that Python ImageConverter pixel description requires both `llm_client` and `llm_model`, while the CLI exposes no flags for those arguments
Offers explicit Azure Content Understanding with `--use-cu`, an endpoint, and Azure authentication as a paid external option that requires user approval
Does not claim that installing `[all]` alone provides local image OCR
